transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Anita Kapoor (Redwood Solutions), Tom Bennett (CTO, Fairfield Trust), Priya Desai (Head of Compliance), Evan Miles (Infra Lead), Sanjay Rao (Security)

[00:00] Laura Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you carving out time. we're gonna run through a quick discovery on data residency and compliance constraints, and then Marco will cover some of the tech details. quick intros?
[00:12] Tom Bennett: Tom Bennett, CTO at Fairfield Trust. we run core banking, online banking, a bunch of customer data is regulated, um so compliance is the main thing for us.
[00:20] Priya Desai: Priya, head of compliance. HIPAA-ish? no, mostly GLBA and state privacy regs and GDPR for our EU customers.
[00:28] Evan Miles: Evan, infra. we manage our AWS accounts, VPCs, some on-prem.
[00:32] Sanjay Rao: Sanjay, security. I'll be asking about keys, access and auditability.
[00:36] Laura Chen: Great, thanks. quick context on Redwood — hosted API is simplest, Dedicated gives reserved capacity in a redwood-managed env, and Private is our VPC / customer-managed control-plane or on-prem option, right Marco?
[00:48] Marco Ruiz: yep, that's right. private gives you a private control plane and can be deployed in your VPC or on prem. dedicated is our reserved GPU pools but still in redwood cloud, so there are different tradeoffs on logs and residency.
[01:05] Tom Bennett: Okay, so top-line — regulators require logs to be retained on-prem or at least exported to our SIEM. They also want access controls and an audit trail that we control. hosted api would be problematic unless we can guarantee EU-only residency for EU customers and control over logs.
[01:24] Priya Desai: Also, some of our examiners have been specific about raw transcripts being present in logs. they don't want PII or account numbers leaking into vendor logs.
[01:35] Laura Chen: Totally. we see that a lot. we support log redaction and can configure retention, but hosted has limits — logs are centralized in our cloud regions and for some customers that's not acceptable.
[01:46] Marco Ruiz: to add, for hosted we can do region pinning, e.g., EU-only model endpoints, but we still manage the control plane and some operational logs live in our environment. For customers who need full control we recommend Private — we can run the control plane in your VPC or provide an on-prem bundle.
[02:05] Evan Miles: If we went Private on VPC, how does KMS work? we need HSM-backed keys, integrated with our AWS KMS or on-prem HSM.
[02:15] Marco Ruiz: we have KMS integration patterns. for private deployments we can plug into customer KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) or integrate with HSMs. there are additional ops notes but it's supported. sometimes customers want envelope encryption so the keys never leave their HSM.
[02:34] Sanjay Rao: Audit logs — can we stream all audit logs to our Splunk / SIEM and set retention on our side? also, is there an option to turn off vendor-side persistent logging of raw prompts?
[02:44] Laura Chen: yes, streaming of audit logs to your SIEM is a common config. and we have options to redact or not persist raw prompts; for Dedicated we can set more restrictive retention policies, and for Private you control it entirely. a caveat: some telemetry required for latency and billing might still be collected unless we do a full private on-prem.
[03:05] Tom Bennett: Billing is fine. regulators want minimal vendor visibility into customer prompts though. can you sign a data processing addendum that clarifies this?
[03:15] Laura Chen: yes, we have a DPA and privacy addendum; we'll include that in the security pack.
[03:19] Priya Desai: GDPR question: data subject requests — do you have APIs for deletion/erasure in our tenancy?
[03:26] Marco Ruiz: for Private deployments the control plane exposes management APIs and you can purge data as you need. for hosted we support deletion endpoints and can backfill with our data retention policies, but timing differs. we'll include specifics in the pack.
[03:40] Evan Miles: Network — if we do Private in our VPC, do you need peering or a transit? how is traffic egress handled?
[03:48] Marco Ruiz: usually we do VPC peering or PrivateLink. egress stays in your VPC if on-prem or customer's cloud. for dedicated in redwood cloud egress exits our region unless you use dedicated private connect options.
[04:02] Sanjay Rao: Any certifications? SOC 2 type II and ISO? our procurement needs those docs.
[04:09] Laura Chen: yes, SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 available; we'll attach certs.
[04:14] Tom Bennett: HIPAA — do you have signed BAAs? we touch health data via certain products.
[04:20] Laura Chen: we do support HIPAA and can sign a BAA for the right deployment model; typically Private or Dedicated with specific controls is required. we'll surface the process in the security pack.
[04:32] Priya Desai: There's also GLBA for financial institutions — we need evidence of encryption at rest, key management, and strong RBAC with SSO integration.
[04:43] Marco Ruiz: RBAC and SSO/SAML are supported; you can restrict access by role, and Private deployments integrate with your IdP. We also provide audit trail per token and per-user.
[05:00] Evan Miles: Latency/cost tradeoff — if we go Private in our region, what impact on latency and cost vs hosted?
[05:08] Marco Ruiz: Private in your region typically reduces latency because the control plane and serving are in-network; cost comes from dedicated infra and ops. hosted is cheapest to start but has the most vendor-managed operations. we can run some benchmarks during the POC to quantify.
[05:28] Tom Bennett: For the POC we need to prove that encrypted traffic and logs meet regulator guidance and that transcripts do not leave our control. also, we want to run a small performance benchmark against our standard 512 token prompts.
[05:42] Laura Chen: makes sense. Marco, we can schedule a POC that focuses on auditability and residency.
[05:47] Marco Ruiz: yes, typical POC: network setup, KMS integration, log streaming to SIEM, and workload run for perf. We'll need your infra diagram and an access window.
[06:00] Priya Desai: One nuance — our state regulator requires that logs containing customer identifiers be retained on-prem for seven years and be available in an unalterable form. is immutable logging supported?
[06:12] Sanjay Rao: also chain-of-custody style controls — can you support write-once logs or forwarding to an immutable store?
[06:18] Marco Ruiz: we support log forwarding to write-once stores (S3 with Object Lock, WORM) for Private deployments; for Dedicated we can configure retention policies and streaming but write-once guarantees depend on the customer's downstream storage if you accept streaming. we'll document both options.
[06:35] Laura Chen: just to be transparent, hosted can't provide the full write-once guarantee in most cases because the vendor's control plane is still in our cloud. for strong regulator needs we recommend Private with your storage.
[06:47] Tom Bennett: Understood. any limitations around model updates — if we pin a model version for production, can that be enforced so new model weights aren't used without change control?
[06:57] Marco Ruiz: yes, we support model pinning and rollout controls; Redwood Console has canary and A/B rollout features. for Private we can lock model versions at the customer level. there might be security patching windows but model weights remain pinned until you approve.
[07:14] Evan Miles: One more — telemetry for billing. can you provide token-level billing but not the actual prompt text? we want to reconcile cost without exposing sensitive prompts.
[07:24] Laura Chen: yes, token-level usage reports are available. those reports can exclude full prompt text; you can get aggregate metrics and per-route breakdowns.
[07:33] Priya Desai: Are there legal restrictions on exporting logs that contain EU personal data to US-based vendors? we need guidance for GDPR cross-border transfers.
[07:42] Marco Ruiz: we support EU data residency and standard contractual clauses for transfers when necessary. for strict requirements we recommend Private in EU region so no cross-border flow. we'll include legal language in the DPA.
[08:00] Tom Bennett: Ok, procurement will want to see evidence that logs can be redacted and that the vendor cannot re-identify data. can you provide details on pseudonymization and redaction tooling?
[08:12] Marco Ruiz: we have a redaction layer that can strip or mask patterns (account numbers, ssn-like) at ingest; for Private you can run it in your network. we'll include examples in the pack.
[08:25] Laura Chen: quick clarifying Q — you mentioned some on-prem components; is Fairfield considering fully on-prem or VPC-hosted private control plane?
[08:33] Tom Bennett: preference is VPC-hosted control plane first. on-prem would be heavier but may be required for certain files.
[08:39] Sanjay Rao: timeline — regulator review in Q2, so we need a POC in the next 4 weeks ideally.
[08:46] Laura Chen: that's doable; we'll try to get the technical deep dive scheduled this week and then a POC kickoff next week.
[08:53] Marco Ruiz: for the POC we'll need a small set of test data, network access, and KMS creds or test keys for integration. we can do perf runs with 512 token prompts and sample concurrency.
[09:06] Evan Miles: Are there known integrations for HSM vendors? we use Thales Luna.
[09:10] Marco Ruiz: Thales and AWS CloudHSM commonly used; we have integration docs.
[09:16] Priya Desai: one blocker — certain examiners object to vendor-managed backups. can backups be stored in our storage only?
[09:24] Marco Ruiz: yes for Private backups can be configured to go to your storage. for Dedicated in our cloud we'd need contract-level guarantees; we'll outline options.
[09:34] Tom Bennett: Good. Any notable limitations in the Private offering around model features — streaming, function calling, tool calls?
[09:44] Marco Ruiz: Private supports streaming and function calls, but some advanced optimizations (specific kernel ops) may vary by hardware. we'll flag those in the POC matrix.
[09:56] Laura Chen: circling back — next steps recap: Laura sends security pack + DPA, Marco schedules technical deep dive, Fairfield shares infra diagram and compliance doc, and we aim to start POC within 4 weeks.
[10:10] Tom Bennett: sounds good. thanks.
[10:14] Priya Desai: thanks, will review docs and confirm stakeholders.
[10:18] Laura Chen: great, we'll follow up with calendar invites. thanks everyone.
